title: Assert SMOKE cases on operator-observable output that proves the acceptance outcome

facts.note: Test file's declared Phase; only SMOKE-phase files are in scope. This plus 'case makes assertions' is the full applicability condition.
Test files under the Bun test runner.

values: bun_tester_discipline_detector: SMOKE case with assertions but no observable channel
facts.note: Detector-specific trigger only (requires the validator run). NOT a prerequisite: cases that do touch a channel (e.g. a generic 200) are still in scope for the semantic obligation.

values: witness does not prove the claimed/bound acceptance outcome
facts.note: Semantic trigger: whether the asserted evidence on the channel is acceptance-specific and would fail on regression; only a reviewer/LLM can judge this.
Whether an acceptance binding exists. Used to select the witness (the bound acceptance's Then), never to exempt unbound asserted SMOKE cases.

fires: A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only on fields of an object the test built itself.
A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only on internal calls or mocks.
A SMOKE-phase test case asserts only a generic HTTP 200 while the bound acceptance promises specific visible content (even though the detector recognizes the channel).
An asserted SMOKE-phase case with no acceptance binding that asserts only on self-built objects.
doesNotFire: A test whose declared Phase is not SMOKE.
A SMOKE case with no assertions at all (owned by other rules).
A SMOKE case asserting acceptance-specific content in the real HTTP response body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, exit code, persisted state, or other operator-observable channel.

given: A test file whose declared Phase is SMOKE contains a case that makes assertions
when: the case's assertions are written or changed
then: At least one assertion must check, on an operator-observable channel (HTTP response status/body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, exit code, persisted state, or other operator-observable channel), the externally visible outcome the case claims — the bound acceptance's Then where one is bound — specifically enough that the case turns red if that behavior disappears.
prefer: Read the acceptance's Then first; identify the externally visible consequence that discharges it.

Exercise the real path and assert on the real HTTP response and its markup (what htmx shows the user), stdout/stderr, exit code, persisted state, or other observable channel: `const res = await fetch("/orders"); expect(res.status).toBe(200); expect(await res.text()).toContain("order-1");` — status is transport evidence; the body check is the acceptance-specific witness.
avoid: Asserting only on objects the test built: `const order = buildOrder({ sku: "x" }); expect(order.sku).toBe("x");` — internal, not SMOKE evidence; it proves the constructor (a unit test's job).
Treating any observable assertion (e.g. a generic `200`) as sufficient when it does not prove the declared outcome.
Checking internal calls or mocks instead of the resulting system behavior.
unless: The case makes no assertions at all — skipped here; other rules own that.
why: The SMOKE label tells the gate real behaviour was exercised, so it must prove something an operator could witness; a self-built object or bare `200` leaves the acceptance (e.g. the new order being visible) unproven.
evidence: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no SMOKE case that makes assertions but touches none of the observable channels.
Reviewer confirms the real path was exercised (real HTTP request/process, not a self-built object or mock).
Reviewer confirms the witness would fail if the bound acceptance behavior regressed (matches the acceptance's Then, not merely 'server answered').
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_tester_discipline_detector (validator). Reports a SMOKE case that makes assertions but touches none of the observable channels.
Scope: only SMOKE-phase files are scanned; cases with no assertions are skipped (other rules own that).

observable_channel vocabulary (Bun/htmx-specific): an HTTP response status or body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, an exit code, or persisted state; the fix hint also admits other observable channels.
self_constructed_object: a value the test built itself; asserting on it proves the constructor works, which is a unit test's job under a SMOKE label.

Division of labour: the detector recognizes the channel only; merely touching a channel is not semantically enough. Whether the evidence on that channel is acceptance-specific (e.g. body contains the created order, not just status 200) is judged by the agent/reviewer. A clean detector result does not establish compliance.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Lineage: Bun realization of the core stack-neutral obligation `tester.smoke.operator-observable-assertion`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun/htmx-specific channel vocabulary.

Re-realized rather than shared because the observable vocabulary is stack-specific: for this stack the canonical observation is often an HTTP response and the markup inside it, because that markup is what htmx puts in front of the user.

sharedNodes.text: strict: the gate fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
